st-louis-turkey-trot-8k-2018.headline: A Thanksgiving reunion I did not expect.

milestone.label: What stood out
milestone.note: Seeing friends and family at Tower Grove Park

memory: I went into the St. Louis Turkey Trot expecting a Thanksgiving morning race in Tower Grove Park, but the thing I remember most is who I found there.
I ran into Leah Forsberg and Chris, and Lindsey Forsberg and Mike. Abby was there with her friend Lauren and Nick, and my mom joined us too.

The surprise of seeing everyone and the happiness of getting to share the morning together is what stayed with me. More than the 8K itself, this race is a memory of an unexpected Thanksgiving reunion.

gobble-cobble-2019.headline: A cold Thanksgiving morning on the Inner Harbor.
memory: I remember being excited for the Gobble Cobble on a pretty cold Thanksgiving morning in Baltimore.
The race was around the Inner Harbor, and the cold weather is one of the clearest things I remember about the morning.
It was a simple, fun Thanksgiving race and another chapter in what eventually became a recurring holiday tradition.

baltimore-virtual-turkey-trot-2020.headline: A virtual Thanksgiving edition in Baltimore.
memory: The 2020 Gobble Cobble was virtual, so this entry is intentionally a short one.
My Thanksgiving Day Strava activity preserves the day: 5.48 kilometers recorded in Baltimore on November 26, 2020.
I do not want to add details I cannot specifically remember, but the activity belongs in the Turkey Trot chronology as the virtual 2020 edition.

mile-high-turkey-trot-2021.headline: A sunny Thanksgiving run with my wife and mom.

milestone.label: Together
milestone.note: Washington Park on a sunny morning

memory: The 2021 Turkey Trot was a sunny day at Washington Park, and I ran it with my wife and my mom.
I remember running well, but the performance is not really what defines the day for me.
What stayed with me was how much fun it was to be there together as a family on Thanksgiving morning.

mile-high-turkey-trot-2023.headline: Running late turned the four-mile race into something longer.
memory: I did the 2023 Turkey Trot at Washington Park with Olive.
We were running late and had to park far from the start, so I ran with Olive from the parking spot just to make it to the race.
That meant the full outing was longer than the nominal four-mile Turkey Trot. The scramble to get there and getting to do the day with Olive are what make this edition memorable.

springfield-turkey-trot-2024.headline: A fun Thanksgiving morning through the UIS campus with Olive.
memory: Olive and I did the Springfield Turkey Trot together on Thanksgiving morning in 2024.
What I remember most is that it was a fun route through the University of Illinois Springfield campus.
The source activity was recorded as a walk, so I do not want to turn it into a performance story. The memory is simply being out there with Olive and enjoying the Thanksgiving event together.

mile-high-turkey-trot-2025.headline: A great Thanksgiving day with Olive at Washington Park.
memory: The 2025 Mile High United Way Turkey Trot brought me back to Washington Park with Olive.
There is not one complicated story I need to attach to this race. I simply remember it as a great day together.
By then, Turkey Trots had become one of those Thanksgiving traditions that connected different places and different years of my life.

mile-high-united-way-turkey-trot-series.headline: Seven Thanksgiving editions that became one tradition.
memory: The Turkey Trots are not one race in one city. They are a Thanksgiving tradition that followed me through St. Louis, Baltimore, Denver, and Springfield.

The memories are different from year to year: an unexpected reunion in St. Louis, a cold morning in Baltimore, a virtual edition in 2020, a sunny family race in Denver, running late with Olive, a Springfield morning through the UIS campus, and another great Washington Park day with Olive in 2025.

Keeping them together as one Story lets the individual races stay intact while showing what connects them: Thanksgiving mornings, family, friends, Olive, and the places I was living or visiting at the time.
